messages:
incident-bot: HIGH queue growth detected for gpu-pool-west-1. metric: inference_queue_length > 500 for 3m. triggering pager S1.

maria (oncall): acked. +1 here, jumping in. seeing 500+ pending requests on the gateway.

alex (infra): looking at autoscaler logs — it hit pool capacity: max_instances=48, current=48, scaling blocked. region quota shows GPUs available but scheduler can't place due to fragmented MIG slices.

julian (sre): confirmed. lots of nodes with small free fragments (1-2GiB equiv); requests want 4xA100-1g MIG units. packer failed earlier (repack-service crashed) so we have stranded slices.

sam (runtime): adding details — model-serving pods are requesting specific MIG shapes: 1g vs 2g mismatches. attempts to fallback to smaller variant fail because model binary isn't compatible. queue backlog grows and runtime is throttling token generation to avoid OOMs.

maria (oncall): customer impact?

cs_lead: several PLG customers reporting >10s response times; 3 paying customers have errors (503). sending notification to CS page.

alex (infra): can we evict non-prod workloads? ops-bot: running suggestion: `reassign-priority --label nonprod --drain --force` recommended.

julian (sre): do it. also enable burst pool if possible. we have a reserved burst-capacity pool but it's offline due to maintenance.

sam (runtime): maintenance window still running, but we can flip the emergency-burst flag. i'll enable it now:

sam (runtime): ```sh
# enable emergency burst pool
./adminctl pools activate --name burst-temp-west --mode emergency
# raise autoscaler soft_limit to 72 temporarily
./autoscaler update-config --pool gpu-pool-west-1 --soft_max 72
```

incident-bot: autoscaler update queued. pool activation in progress (async job id: job-7892).

alex (infra): repack-service logs show OOM on 2024-11-15T03:12:10Z then crashloop. restarting with extra memory.

julian (sre): manual mitigations while repack comes up: 1) evict labelled noncritical; 2) fallback routing to cpu-fallback for low-priority customers; 3) temporary MIG-resize on a subset of nodes to consolidate free slots. we should pick a small subset to avoid churn.

maria (oncall): do eviction now. which customers get CPU fallback?

cs_lead: choose internal/non-urgent experimental tenants + free-tier customers first. notify customers in parallel.

sam (runtime): eviction command sent: `kubectl label pod -l tier=noncritical evict-now=true && kubectl delete pods -l evict-now=true --grace-period=30` — started.

ops-bot: 12 non-prod pods evicted, freed 4 MIG slices. queue down to 420.

alex (infra): burst pool activation succeeded, 8 extra instances provisioned but scheduler still can't place because of mismatched MIG slice sizes on nodes.

julian (sre): i'm running a focused repack on 6 nodes: `repack-tool --node-set node-22,node-23,node-45,node-46,node-47,node-48 --strategy consolidate --force`

sam (runtime): repack-tool output (excerpt):
```
repack-start node-22
migrating 2 pods -> node-46
adjusting MIG sizes: node-23: 2x1g -> 1x2g (requires drain)
repack-complete node-22..47: freed 6x1g fragments
```

maria (oncall): queue now 160 and trending down. customer errors dropping. keep monitoring.

cs_lead: notifying affected customers with status update: we routed low-priority traffic to CPU fallback and elevated high-priority to burst pool. SLA impact estimated: degraded latency for 3 customers for ~30m, 503s for 2 customers for ~12m.

julian (sre): root cause summary so far: repack-service OOM/crash prevented automated consolidation; MIG-size heterogeneity + previous packing strategy led to fragmentation; autoscaler hit hard cap before repack could free contiguous slices.

alex (infra): temporary fixes applied: restarted repack-service with larger heap, forced repack on hot nodes, evicted nonprod, activated burst pool, raised soft limits.

maria (oncall): are we safe to demote to postmortem? any open tasks blocking recovery?

sam (runtime): still one small pool with mismatched slices; i'm running a rolling MIG-resize on it but that can take ~8-10m. will update.

julian (sre): assign follow-ups: (a) autoscaler should prefer soft scaling to avoid hitting hard cap when fragmentation > 30% (owner: alex), (b) repack-service needs HA + OOM safety (owner: julian), (c) add eval in CI for mixed MIG shapes to ensure fallback compatibility (owner: sam), (d) improve customer-visible gradations instead of outright 503 (owner: cs_lead).

maria (oncall): thanks team. reassigning incident to postmortem channel. closing live thread once final metrics look stable. :white_check_mark:
